SMTO-CFG-0066 — This action no longer matches the task's saved settings

GUID: e9de32ee-c17b-427f-ad09-31dc35e7af8f
Slug: policy-snapshot-changed
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A setting changed after this task started. Either a different Behavior effort was requested than the task started with, or the Unsafe actions setting changed just before SMTO asked for your approval.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see which message you got: Behavior effort differs, or Unsafe action policy changed. Each of these has a different fix.
  2. For Behavior effort: retry or continue the task with its original effort. To use a different effort, start a new task and choose it under Behavior effort first. A task keeps the Behavior effort it started with, so a different one can't be applied to it.
  3. For Unsafe action policy: open Settings › Security and check that Unsafe actions is set as you want (Ask, Run blindly or Disallow). Then ask SMTO to do the operation again. The setting changed before SMTO could ask you, so it stopped instead of running the operation.

What success looks like

  • The task runs with the effort you chose, or SMTO follows your current Unsafe actions setting, for example by showing a new approval prompt.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select Proceed on an approval prompt that was open before the setting changed; refresh the page and ask again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A captured-policy check failed: the requested behavior_effort differs from the task's captured behavior policy, or an unsafe-action approval challenge was requested after unsafe_action_policy changed from ask.

What this means

  • A requested behavior effort differs from its immutable policy snapshot, or an unsafe approval challenge is requested when current unsafe policy is no longer ask. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • A requested behavior effort differs from its immutable policy snapshot, or an unsafe approval challenge is requested when current unsafe policy is no longer ask.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish captured behavior mismatch from current unsafe-policy change before choosing a settings scope.

How to fix it

  • For behavior effort, submit the task's captured effort (apply_behavior_policy rejects a differing effort) or create a new task with the new effort. For unsafe actions, read the current unsafe_action_policy (Settings > Security > Unsafe actions; UnsafeAuthority.policy) and request the operation again so a new decision is made under it; never reuse a stale challenge ID.
  • Inspect the specific owning policy. Keep accepted behavior snapshots intact and request unsafe work only through its current policy controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • New behavior uses an eligible new snapshot; unsafe work follows the current explicit approval policy.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
